edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 for the Shares, payable in full at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by the Seller.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 30 days of signing, on a date mutually agreed in writing by the parties, subject to receipt of any legally required regulatory approvals. Transfer of the Shares and payment of the Purchase Price shall occur concurrently.

3. Representations. Except as disclosed in writing to the Buyer before signing, the Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company for the dates and periods covered, in accordance with the accounting principles identified in those statements, consistently applied, subject, in the case of unaudited statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the terms of this Agreement confidential and shall not disclose them without the other party's prior written consent, except to its professional advisers and financing sources who are subject to confidentiality obligations, or as required by applicable law or legal process. To the extent legally permitted, a party required to make disclosure shall give the other party prompt prior notice and disclose only what is legally required.

Make a materially lower counteroffer without claiming unsupported valuation facts, while preserving diligence and approval conditions. Seek stronger financial-statement protection and a workable closing timetable.

receiver.requested_changes: Revise Section 1 to provide a USD 35,000,000 purchase price, payable at Closing, subject to agreement on customary cash, debt, transaction-expense, and working-capital adjustments. Require independently verified wire instructions and delivery of shares free of liens. Revise Section 2 so Closing occurs within 30 days after signing only if agreed closing conditions are satisfied or waived, including legally required approvals; agree an appropriate outside date and termination rights. In Section 3, limit disclosure exceptions to a specific disclosure schedule delivered and agreed before signing, rather than any prior written disclosure. Require identification of the applicable accounting principles, limit unaudited year-end adjustments to nonmaterial adjustments, and add appropriate representations concerning undisclosed liabilities, title, authority, taxes, and material contracts, together with negotiated survival and indemnification provisions. Retain Section 4 substantially as drafted, but permit confidential disclosures to the parties’ relevant personnel and representatives on a need-to-know basis under appropriate confidentiality obligations.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The proposed purchase price for the Shares is USD 40,000,000, subject to Seller approval and agreement on customary cash, debt, unpaid transaction-expense and working-capital adjustments. Before signing, the parties shall agree definitions, the working-capital target, accounting policies, a sample calculation, preparation and review procedures, and resolution of disputed adjustment items by an independent accountant acting as expert. Adjustments shall avoid double counting. The estimated adjusted Purchase Price shall be payable in full at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the Seller's designated account, with a post-Closing true-up under those procedures. The Buyer shall independently verify the Seller's wire instructions, and any changes, by callback to a previously authenticated Seller contact using independently established contact details. Payment and delivery of the Shares, free and clear of liens and with duly executed transfer instruments, shall occur concurrently.

2. Closing. The parties shall target Closing within 30 days after signing, on a mutually agreed date, provided the agreed closing conditions have been satisfied or, where legally permissible, waived by the party entitled to their benefit. Conditions shall include legally required approvals, absence of any legal prohibition, performance in all material respects of pre-Closing covenants, accuracy of representations subject to agreed materiality standards, and delivery of the agreed Closing documents. Diligence shall be completed to the Buyer's satisfaction before signing; no discretionary diligence or financing condition shall apply after signing unless expressly agreed. Each party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to satisfy the conditions applicable to it. The proposed outside date is 60 days after signing, extendable by written agreement. Either party may terminate by written notice if Closing has not occurred by the outside date, unless that party's material breach caused the failure to close; either party may also terminate for a final, nonappealable legal prohibition or the other party's material breach that prevents satisfaction of a closing condition and remains uncured for 15 days after written notice. The parties may terminate by mutual written agreement. Termination shall not affect accrued liability for pre-termination breach, and confidentiality shall survive.

3. Representations and Indemnification. Exceptions to the Seller's representations shall be limited to a specific disclosure schedule delivered to and agreed with the Buyer before signing, identifying the representation qualified; cross-disclosure shall apply only where its relevance is reasonably apparent on its face. Other prior communications shall not qualify the representations. The definitive agreement shall identify the applicable accounting principles expressly before signing. Subject to that schedule, the Seller shall represent at signing and Closing that: (a) the identified financial statements fairly present, in all material respects, the Company's financial position and results for the dates and periods covered in accordance with those accounting principles, consistently applied, subject, for unaudited statements, only to normal, nonmaterial year-end adjustments and absence of footnotes; (b) the Company has no liabilities required to be reflected or reserved under those principles other than those reflected or reserved in the identified statements, incurred in the ordinary course since their balance-sheet date, or arising under the transaction documents; (c) the Seller owns the Shares and will transfer good title free of liens; (d) the Seller has authority to execute and perform the agreement, which constitutes its binding obligation subject to customary enforceability exceptions; (e) the Company has timely filed all material required tax returns, those returns are materially accurate, all material taxes due have been paid or properly reserved, and no material tax dispute is pending or, to the Seller's knowledge, threatened in writing; and (f) the schedule identifies all material contracts under agreed criteria, each is in force subject to customary enforceability exceptions, the Company is not in material default, and, to the Seller's knowledge, no counterparty is in material default. The Buyer shall give reciprocal authority and enforceability representations and represent that it has sufficient immediately available funds at Closing.
The proposed indemnification framework is as follows: general representations survive for 18 months after Closing; title and authority representations survive for six years; and tax representations survive until 60 days after expiration of the applicable statutory limitation period. Claims notified with reasonable particulars before expiration survive until resolved. The Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for direct losses arising from breaches of Seller representations and covenants and pre-Closing Company taxes under an agreed tax covenant, without duplicate recovery. General representation claims shall be subject to a USD 25,000 per-claim de minimis, a deductible basket equal to 1% of the final Purchase Price and an aggregate cap of 10% of that price. Title, authority and tax claims shall be excluded from the de minimis, basket and general cap but subject to an aggregate cap equal to the final Purchase Price. Covenant liability shall be addressed expressly in the definitive agreement. Recovery shall be reduced by actual insurance recoveries and actual tax benefits, net of reasonable recovery costs, and subject to reasonable mitigation. No recovery shall be available for amounts already reflected in the price adjustments. Third-party claims shall be subject to prompt notice, protection against prejudice from delayed notice, appropriate defense control and no settlement imposing admissions or nonmonetary obligations on the indemnified party without its consent. Indemnification shall be the exclusive post-Closing monetary remedy except for fraud by the party against whom relief is sought; equitable relief shall remain available. No limitation shall protect a party against its own fraud.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the terms of this Agreement confidential and shall not disclose them without the other party's prior written consent, except on a need-to-know basis to its relevant personnel, professional advisers, financing sources and other representatives who are bound by appropriate contractual or professional confidentiality obligations, or as required by applicable law or legal process. Each party shall be responsible for compliance with this provision by persons to whom it discloses the terms. To the extent legally permitted, a party required to make disclosure shall give the other party prompt prior notice and disclose only what is legally required.

receiver.message_back:
Thank you. The revised draft is a constructive step on mechanics and risk allocation. Subject to contract, satisfactory diligence, Buyer approval and agreement of definitive terms, our client maintains its proposal of USD 35,000,000, payable at Closing subject to agreed cash, debt, unpaid transaction-expense and working-capital adjustments. We do not accept the USD 40,000,000 counterproposal.

We can work from the revised payment-verification, concurrent unencumbered transfer, specific-disclosure and confidentiality provisions. Before signing, we must settle the accounting framework, working-capital target, illustrative calculation and complete adjustment procedures, including access to supporting records and the independent accountant's remit.

The closing framework is broadly workable, subject to appropriate ordinary-course and no-leakage covenants, access and notice obligations, an agreed material-adverse-effect condition and review of approval timing. We acknowledge that diligence is to be completed before signing and are not proposing a discretionary post-signing diligence condition.

The representation package needs to be completed following diligence, including capitalization, compliance, litigation, employment and benefits, intellectual property, privacy/cybersecurity, assets and related-party matters where applicable.

On indemnification, we propose 24-month general survival, a USD 10,000 de minimis, a 0.5% tipping basket and a 20% general cap. Fundamental and tax claims should remain outside those thresholds and the general cap. Covenant liability must be separately specified rather than left subject to uncertain limits. The direct-loss-only restriction is not acceptable: reasonably foreseeable consequential losses and covered third-party liabilities should not be categorically excluded. We also require an agreed pre-Closing tax covenant and propose a 10% escrow from Closing proceeds for 24 months, retaining amounts needed for timely notified unresolved claims. The exclusive-remedy provision remains subject to agreement on the complete remedies package.

Please seek Seller instructions on the USD 35,000,000 proposal and these remaining points. No binding agreement arises unless and until definitive documents are agreed and executed.
